column1: # THE ROSARIO DEATH INDEX - opened for the first time, 13 September 2026.
# "Indice de defunciones 1800-1888", Parroquia Nuestra Senora del Rosario, via the FamilySearch
# waypoint browse (cc=1974196). EIGHTY-SIX IMAGES. HANDWRITTEN, not the 1945 typescript - four
# columns to a page, surname / given name / folio, grouped by letter and then by libro and year.
# WHY IT MATTERS: a death act names the parents of the deceased. If Juan Carlos Lerena or Maria
# Lerena died at Rosario, this is where they would be. In six days of work nobody had opened it.
# *** THE VOLUME IS A COMPOSITE. *** It is not one index. Bound together, in this order:
#   images 3-44   DEATH INDEX, first sequence: A to Z, libros 4-7, covering 1800-1839.
#   images 45-53  DEATH INDEX, second sequence: "Letra A" to "Letra S", covering 1882-1888.
#   images ~51-55 A further index in which entries read "X con Y" - MARRIAGES, not deaths.
#   images 56-58  "BAUTISMOS DE LOS YNDIOS" - an index of indigenous baptisms, letters A-P.
#   images 59-86  DEATH INDEX, third sequence: libros 4-8, c.1838-1869 - AND IT STOPS AT F.

column1: # *** THE RESULT, STATED PLAINLY. ***
# 1. For 1800-1839 and for 1882-1888, the Rosario death index has been read end to end under L.
#    THERE IS NO LERENA IN EITHER.
# 2. For roughly 1840 to 1881 THERE IS NO L SECTION TO READ. The index that covers those years
#    breaks off at the letter F. This is not a gap in the searching - it is a gap in the record.
# What that means for the central question: if Juan Carlos Lerena or Maria Lerena died at Rosario
# between 1840 and 1881 - which is exactly the window in which a parent of an 1882 child would be
# most likely to die - the finding aid that would locate them DOES NOT EXIST. The death REGISTERS
# for 1841-1875 do survive and are filmed; they would have to be read act by act, which is a far
# larger job than the index would have been, and is now the only route.
# A NOTE ON METHOD: this index is handwritten and dense. Level 12 at 0.58 scale, one page-half per
# screenshot, proved the reliable setting; level 13 is sharper but drops tiles on this film.
